result.short_description: Issue in website www.telerik.com
result.description: Hello, I noticed in the last few days that the Sitefinity backend for both Progress.com and Telerik.com was updated to Sitefinity 11.2. First, this is great! :). Second, there have been some apparent side effects - the RSS feed for both the Progress.com and Telerik.com blogs have been affected and now show seemingly random historical posts in the current feed, burying actually recent posts from a few days ago. In addition to this affecting our many RSS subscribers, our blog newsletters are based on this feed and are unable to discover this content as it has been pushed off the feed entirely. https://feeds.telerik.com/blogs http://feeds.progress.com/blogs I have two questions here: 1) Is there any way to restore the feed, so that posts are in their proper order by publication date? If this can be done fairly quickly, we would be able to include any currently buried content in our next weekly newsletter send. This would also minimize disruption for our RSS subscribers. 2) Are there any further planned Sitefinity updates that may affect the blog that we should be aware of? Thanks! (I'm also generally quite interested in what benefits the new version of Sitefinity may bring to the blog - I've already seen some changes just in the course of my daily activities. I don't want to overburden this ticket but I'd love to find out more.)
result.close_notes:
1) I just spent a while digging into the last few weeks worth of posts and something unusual is going on - but hopefully I have resolved it for the purposes of the RSS feed, at least:

1a) Historically, the only way I have been able to alter the feed is by explicitly republishing with a new publication date. I tried manually saving a new draft of a post without republishing it just to update the modification date, but that had no effect on the RSS feed. 
1b) I then tried republishing the same post, again without a new publication date, and this time it inserted itself into the RSS feed - not the top, but about 5 down, which is where it should have been based on its original publication date.
1c) I then went through the last 2 weeks of content in the backend and hit "publish" from the More Actions dropdown to try and reset the placement of this content. However, despite the backend showing a publication date of today, the publication date on each post reverted to the timestamp from which they were originally uploaded into the backend - sometimes months earlier.
1d) I then opened each post individually, selecting "publish on specific date" from the dropdown, and the correct timestamp from when it was actually published was automatically populated, so I hit save for each one
1e) After this last step, each post I republished is now displaying in the correct order on both the live blog page AND the RSS feed.

The original issue, I believe, was that due to the Sitefinity update, all blog content prior to 4/24 was given a "last modified" timestamp of approximately 4/24/19 at 05:41, and the ordering did not align to when they were originally published. It looks like there may have been some other quirks due to the migration as well, as in the conflicting publication dates above.

In any case, hopefully this is resolved! And I hope that my accounting of it is useful in terms of understanding any bugs that the migration may have caused.
result.comments:
26-Apr-19 14:40:32 - Daniel Shain (Additional comments)
Hi Kristian, 

1) I just spent a while digging into the last few weeks worth of posts and something unusual is going on - but hopefully I have resolved it for the purposes of the RSS feed, at least:

1a) Historically, the only way I have been able to alter the feed is by explicitly republishing with a new publication date. I tried manually saving a new draft of a post without republishing it just to update the modification date, but that had no effect on the RSS feed. 
1b) I then tried republishing the same post, again without a new publication date, and this time it inserted itself into the RSS feed - not the top, but about 5 down, which is where it should have been based on its original publication date.
1c) I then went through the last 2 weeks of content in the backend and hit "publish" from the More Actions dropdown to try and reset the placement of this content. However, despite the backend showing a publication date of today, the publication date on each post reverted to the timestamp from which they were originally uploaded into the backend - sometimes months earlier.
1d) I then opened each post individually, selecting "publish on specific date" from the dropdown, and the correct timestamp from when it was actually published was automatically populated, so I hit save for each one
1e) After this last step, each post I republished is now displaying in the correct order on both the live blog page AND the RSS feed.

The original issue, I believe, was that due to the Sitefinity update, all blog content prior to 4/24 was given a "last modified" timestamp of approximately 4/24/19 at 05:41, and the ordering did not align to when they were originally published. It looks like there may have been some other quirks due to the migration as well, as in the conflicting publication dates above.

In any case, hopefully this is resolved! And I hope that my accounting of it is useful in terms of understanding any bugs that the migration may have caused.

2) Thanks, good to know.

3) Interesting! I'll be curious to see how you're implementing these social/mobile/content editor changes - improvements or new features for any of these aspects would be welcome! :)

Thanks,
-Danny

26-Apr-19 12:42:32 - Kristian Kirov (Additional comments)
Hi Danny,

1) Sitefinity only supports ordering of items in RSS by last modification date so the blog posts are and even before the version upgrade were order by modification date, not by publication date. 

When I filter the published blog posts and sort them by modification date, in the backend, I see exactly the same posts in exactly the same order. View the attachment to see how you can do this.

2) There are no recent planned upgrades

3) This are some of the features that we plan to gradually enable and are related to the blog posts:
- Enable Open Graph properties for blogs: https://www.progress.com/documentation/sitefinity-cms/open-graph-settings
- Migrate our custom AMP implementation the the built-in implementation that should provide better support: https://www.progress.com/documentation/sitefinity-cms/mobile-formats
- Enable new content editing experience for blogs: https://www.progress.com/documentation/sitefinity-cms/new-content-editing-experience
